title: AlGaAs nanowires as a universal platform for GaAs, InGaAs, and InAs quantum dots
authors: Rohan Radhakrishnan, Rodion Reznik, Gilles Patriarche, Igor Ilkiv, Konstantin Kotlyar, Anna Andreeva, George Cirlin, Nika Akopian
abstract: Optical quantum dots (QDs) are central to photonic quantum technologies, with fabrication approaches tailored to different spectral ranges. A key challenge, however, is the realization of a unified platform$\unicode{x2014}$a single growth method combined with a host material offering a designable architecture$\unicode{x2014}$enabling wavelength tunability across the full emission range and co-integration of multiple quantum dots. Here, we introduce AlGaAs nanowires as a universal host for GaAs, InGaAs, and InAs QDs. Building on our previous demonstration of high-quality GaAs QDs, we realize InGaAs QDs with tunable emission by varying the growth duration from 2 to 5 s, achieving emission at 780 and 920 nm. We further showcase the platform's versatility for multi-quantum-dot devices by co-integrating two InGaAs QDs, as well as GaAs and InGaAs QDs within a single nanowire. Finally, we initiate a first step toward pure InAs QDs by growing a pristine InAs segment on AlGaAs nanowires, demonstrating material compatibility.
summary: The authors introduce AlGaAs nanowires as a universal platform for fabricating and characterizing quantum dots made of GaAs, InGaAs, and InAs. By precisely controlling the growth process, they achieve deterministic tuning of the emission wavelength and successfully co-integrate different materials into single devices. This establishes a crucial building block for scalable, on-chip quantum light sources.
main_problem: The challenge is to create a single, universal platform for optical quantum dots (QDs) that allows for wavelength tunability across a broad spectral range and enables the co-integration of multiple different QD materials.
main_result: AlGaAs nanowires are successfully demonstrated as a universal host material capable of growing and characterizing multiple QD types (GaAs, InGaAs, InAs) with tunable emission wavelengths and confirmed single-photon emission.
method: The research employs Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) for growth, coupled with advanced optical characterization techniques like micro-photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, polarization measurements, and cross-correlation measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the AlGaAs nanowire acting as a host matrix for embedded semiconductor quantum dots (InGaAs, GaAs, InAs). The study investigates the excitonic and biexcitonic transitions within these confined structures.
key_observables: QD emission wavelength (tunable from $\sim 780 	ext{ nm}$ to $\sim 920 	ext{ nm}$), single-photon statistics ($g_2(0) \approx 0$), fine-structure splitting, and the observation of multiple excitonic transitions (X, XX, CX).
important_parameters: Growth time (used to tune emission wavelength), QD height, and the material composition (GaAs, InGaAs, InAs).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the AlGaAs nanowire structure provides a stable and controllable template for integrating disparate semiconductor materials into functional quantum emitters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the tunability of PL spectra across different growth times, confirm single-photon emission via cross-correlation, and show structural evidence (STEM/EDX) of pure InAs segments grown on the nanowire.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the basic tunability of InGaAs QDs, then demonstrating the versatility by co-integrating multiple QD types (e.g., GaAs/InGaAs), and finally extending the platform's capability to include pure InAs segments, confirming material compatibility across the full GaAs-InAs range.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware requirements for quantum networking by providing a scalable, multi-material platform for generating on-demand, spectrally tunable single-photon sources.
